column1: # The coverage ratchet baseline — doc:35-testing#coverage.
# module, missed instructions, missed branches, covered instructions, covered branches.
# All four figures are EXACT bounds: the build fails when a module's count differs from
# its row in either direction, so both halves of the ratio move only through this file.
# Regenerate with ./gradlew coverageBaselineWrite, and review the diff. The writer
# REFUSES to raise a missed count; a deliberate regression needs
# -Pcoverage.regress=<reason>, and the reason is recorded below.

# REGRESSION accepted with -Pcoverage.regress: identity validators replaced two three-branch isNotBlank() && none{} checks with single whole-string regex matches; six branches disappear from the source, none become uncovered (missed branches stay 0)
#   :core-domain: covered branches 44 -> 38

# REGRESSION accepted with -Pcoverage.regress: GrantIssued stores its capabilities as a Set rather than a List, so three toSet() calls disappear from equals, hashCode and the field initialiser; six instructions leave the source, none become uncovered (missed instructions stay 0)
#   :core-domain: covered instructions 1549 -> 1543

# REGRESSION accepted with -Pcoverage.regress: PathLocks moved its stripe map from an instance field to the companion object so two DocumentStore instances over one root share one lock (bean:0147 criterion 8); the per-instance field initialiser leaves the source, none of its instructions become uncovered (missed instructions stay 0)
#   :adapter-persistence-flatfile: covered instructions 780 -> 778
# Restored by hand in bean:0032, bean:0030, twice in bean:0036, again in bean:0065 and
# twice in bean:0147 after coverageBaselineWrite erased it; it also erases a PREVIOUS
# regression block when recording a new one. bean:0065 is the cleanest instance yet: the
# writer destroyed all six lines on a run in which NO figure changed, because it rebuilds
# the file from a constant header plus rows and the note it composes is empty unless THIS
# run regressed. bean:0147 saw both halves in one branch: its first write did not regress
# and the block went anyway, and its second DID regress and erased the two older blocks
# while writing its own — so a regression is recorded at the cost of every regression
# before it. bean:0033 makes it survive.
